exp: At 15,000 ft the ISA temperature is -15 C, so the air is ISA. Relative density there is about 0.629, so TAS = CAS / sqrt(0.629) = 145 / 0.793 = 183 kt.

q: The velocity of the speed of sound at sea level in the standard atmosphere is?
exp: Local speed of sound (kt) = 38.94 x square root of absolute temperature (K). ISA temperature = 15 - 1.98 C per 1000 ft. At sea level ISA (288.15 K): 38.94 x 16.98 = 661 kt.

q: An aircraft flying at FL310 is cruising at a CAS of 280 Kts. If the correct outside air temperature is -48°C, this will give a mach number of?
exp: Mach number follows from CAS and pressure altitude alone. At FL310 (static pressure 287 hPa), 280 kt CAS gives an impact pressure of about 133 hPa, which corresponds to Mach 0.76. The temperature is not needed.

q: An aircraft is flying at 1100 Kts TAS at FL650. A change of 0.1M gives a change of 57 Kts TAS. The temperature deviation at FL650 assuming an ISA atmosphere is?
exp: Local speed of sound (kt) = 38.94 x square root of absolute temperature (K). ISA temperature = 15 - 1.98 C per 1000 ft. 0.1 M = 57 kt, so the speed of sound is 570 kt and T = (570 / 38.94)^2 = 214.3 K = -58.9 C. ISA at FL650 is -56.5 C, so the deviation is about -2.5.

q: An aircraft is flying at FL290 at 500 Kts TAS, 0.86M, the temperature deviation is?

q: An increase of 0.15 in mach number results in an increase of 93 Kts TAS. If temperature deviation from ISA is +9°C, the FL is?
